title: What Is LegislationPatch? Plain-English Bill Tracking Explained

sources.label: LegislationPatch site-facts sheet — countable claims derived from the repository by scripts/generate-site-facts.js
scripts/fetch_vote_data.js — roll-call fetch and crossover detection
scripts/fetch_bill_cr.js — the bill-page Congressional Record quote extractor
scripts/fetch_bills_data.js — bill text and metadata fetch, and the version ladder
scripts/prompts.js — the drafting prompts and quality rules

claims.claim: Bill text is pulled directly from an official government source rather than from an aggregator.

claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Summaries mostly run one to three sentences; 28 of the 219 run longer.
claims.sourceSpan: Plain-English summary length per bill: range 1 to 15 sentences; 28 of 219 bills run to more than three.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Top-line counts run one to nine, with 35 of the 219 bills carrying four or more.
claims.sourceSpan: Top-line change counts per bill: range 1 to 9; 35 of 219 bills carry more than three.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Top lines lead with the dollar amounts, thresholds and deadlines the bill text states.
claims.sourceSpan: Lead with the dollar amount, percentage, threshold, or deadline when the source has one.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Every figure in an analysis must trace to the source text, never to memory.
claims.sourceSpan: Estimating, guessing, rounding to a vague figure, or recalling from memory is NEVER allowed.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Congressional quotes are verbatim from the Record, not paraphrased and not taken from a press release.
claims.sourceSpan: // Every sentence of the quote must appear verbatim in the CR
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Crossover votes are flagged only where the margin was within 30% of total yeas plus nays.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: 68 of the 219 bills have been signed into law, so only those are eligible to show enrolled text.
claims.sourceSpan: Bills signed into law (stage signed), and so eligible to show enrolled text: 68 of 219
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: 73 of the 151 non-enacted bills are showing an older version than Congress.gov now lists.
claims.sourceSpan: Bills whose stored text is OLDER than the newest version their own versions[] lists as posted: 73 of 151 non-enacted bills.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Two of the 68 enacted bills are still showing the text as introduced.
claims.sourceSpan: Enacted bills whose stored text is still the version as introduced: 2 (119-S-1003, 119-S-629)
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: An already-cached bill that advances is not automatically re-fetched.
claims.sourceSpan: an already-cached bill that advances is not automatically re-fetched.
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: At fetch time the pipeline prefers enrolled, then engrossed amendment, engrossed, reported, and only then introduced.
claims.sourceSpan: (Enrolled > Engrossed Amendment > Engrossed > Reported > Introduced), tie-broken
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: The bill page labels that panel "Full Bill Text", not "enrolled".
claims.sourceSpan: Bill-text panel label rendered by bill.js: "Full Bill Text"
claims.section: What the Site Actually Shows You

claims.claim: Coverage is selective: 107 bills are deliberately excluded from analysis.
claims.sourceSpan: Bills deliberately excluded from analysis in data/analysis-skip.json: 107

claims.claim: The excluded bills are 29 ceremonial, 28 deferred-minor, 27 procedural and 23 CRA disapproval resolutions.
claims.sourceSpan: Excluded bills by category: 29 ceremonial, 28 deferred-minor, 27 procedural, 23 cra-disapproval

claims.claim: Resolutions of disapproval reach the floor by design, so a claim to track everything with floor action would be false.
claims.sourceSpan: The cra-disapproval category covers resolutions of disapproval, which reach the floor by design; they are excluded from analysis, so coverage is not "all legislation with floor action".

claims.claim: The Holocaust art example is a real published analysis: the bill removes procedural defenses in Holocaust art restitution cases.
claims.sourceSpan: It prohibits courts from dismissing Holocaust art claims based on the passage of time or other procedural defenses

claims.claim: The named defenses removed are laches, adverse possession, international comity, forum non conveniens and act of state.
claims.sourceSpan: Laches, adverse possession, international comity, forum non conveniens, and act of state doctrine may no longer be used to dismiss Holocaust art claims
